label: Disease context
description: Prioritize diseases, conditions, and phenotypic themes most strongly supported by the molecular findings, while keeping mechanistic and clinical claims conservative.
intent: Use this when the user wants the report to focus on which diseases or conditions best fit the genes, pathways, signatures, or omics findings.

sections.heading: Question and Disease Scope
sections.guidance: State the biological question, the molecular findings under review, and which diseases or condition families are in scope.

sections.heading: Dominant Disease Themes
sections.guidance: Summarize the diseases, conditions, or phenotype programs most strongly supported by current enrichment, association, and literature evidence.

sections.heading: Supporting Molecular Findings
sections.guidance: Tie the leading disease themes back to the strongest genes, pathways, signatures, or omics patterns that support them.

sections.heading: Condition-Level Evidence
sections.guidance: Differentiate broad disease programs from more specific named conditions, and explain how strong or weak the condition-level support is.

sections.heading: Competing or Secondary Disease Interpretations
sections.guidance: List plausible alternative disease themes, overlaps, or confounders that could explain parts of the signal.

sections.heading: Clinical and Biological Boundaries
sections.guidance: State clearly what the current evidence does and does not justify, especially around diagnosis, causality, stratification, or actionability.

sections.heading: Next Disease-Focused Checks
sections.guidance: Suggest the next lookups, datasets, comparisons, or validations that would strengthen or falsify the leading disease interpretation.
